subject: Day 8: insurance enrollment confirmed; feed-and-sleep rhythm
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 8. Weight should be climbing 0.5-1 oz per day from here through day 14. The feed-and-sleep rhythm is stabilizing into a 2-3 hour cycle (breastfeeding) or 3-4 hour cycle (formula). Avi can produce roughly 8-12 wet diapers per day now. Cluster feeding in the evening is still normal and not a deficit signal.

Action items
- Call your health insurance company today to verify Avi's enrollment processed. The form is not the same as enrollment. The 1-month well visit needs active coverage. Healthcare.gov reference on qualifying life events: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- If the first-week weight check has not happened, call the pediatrician this morning. Day 8 is past the recommended window. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Continue the feeding log; one more week of data will give the pediatrician a clean picture at the 1-month visit.
- Order another 4-6 weeks of postpartum supplies for the mother. Lochia is still in the rubra-to-serosa transition; pad volume runs out faster than expected. ACOG postpartum care overview: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- If you have not started a baby photo backup routine, set one up today. Apple Photos shared album or Google Photos partner sharing both work. Daily routine: one photo per day.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump still attached and drying. Mustard-yellow or tan stool. Cluster feeding 60-90 minutes in the evening. Faint baby acne peaking around days 7-14.
- [low concern] Mother's bleeding lighter than three days ago.
- [monitor] Cord stump weeping or surrounding skin slightly red. Mother's bleeding suddenly heavier or with large clots.
- [call within 24h] Pus, foul smell, or redness extending more than 1 cm around the cord (omphalitis is rare but emergent). Yellow tinge still spreading. Fewer than six wet diapers in a day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C) in an infant under 90 days. Lethargy, refusal of all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Tummy time on a parent's chest accumulating 5-10 minutes total today. Counter-positions the natural side-preference that develops when newborns spend most time supine. AAP HealthyChildren on back-to-sleep and tummy-to-play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt; expect 24-48 hours of feeding-frequency uptick.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.

Further reading
- AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time and back-to-sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- ACOG on the postpartum period (week 1-6): https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-based decisions: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
